text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Sunday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Palestinian Authority to United States: Press Israel to implement Hebron pact.
- Hizbollah guerrillas vow to retaliate for shooting in Lebanon. 12 Lebanese civilians injured in Israeli army attack.

- Egyptian, Jordanian ties still on ice. Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak won't meet Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu until Hebron solution is reached. Silence continues between Netanyahu, King Hussein.
- Cabinet to discuss Brodett Committee report today on reform of capital markets, including aim to divert short-term savings into long-term alternatives.
- Political cabinet meets today to discuss opening the Solomon Stables mosque. Shimon Peres will meet Yasser Arafat today at request of the Palestinian Authority chairman.
- A majority of cabinet ministers will oppose Brodett Committee recommendation to impose a tax on savings.
- About half of the Arab families in Israel live under the poverty line -- 62 percent of the Arab children.
- Political sources: "The Hebron redeployment -- in the next two weeks."
- 33 officers and fighters tell Netanyahu: "You're dragging us into war".
- Arab leaders boycott Netanyahu until "the evacuation of Hebron". Egypt, Jordan, Tunisia, Morocco and Qatar refuse to meet the prime minister though they'll meet other Israeli representatives.
- Agriculture Minister Rafael Eitan says there is a need for an emergency government -- "because of the economic crisis".
